Safeguarding Champion Role Guidance

*Supersedes the version effective 1 June 2025. 'Safeguarding lead' renamed to 'Safeguarding champion' throughout — the role and its responsibilities are unchanged.*

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains the safeguarding champion role at each Alderbridge site. It applies to every registered manager deciding who to nominate.

Policy statement

Each site nominates a safeguarding champion who acts as the first point of contact for safeguarding questions, providing local expertise and support to colleagues raising a concern.

Definitions

**Safeguarding champion** the Level 3 trained staff member nominated at each site as the local point of safeguarding expertise, renamed in this version from the previous term 'safeguarding lead' — the role itself is unchanged. **First point of contact** the role of being the person a colleague approaches first with a safeguarding question or concern, before wider escalation.

1. Nominate a staff member holding, or willing to complete, Level 3 safeguarding training as the site's safeguarding champion.
2. Make the safeguarding champion's identity clearly known to every staff member, including on the site's safeguarding noticeboard, updated to reflect the new title.
3. Support the safeguarding champion to attend the wider Alderbridge safeguarding network meeting, sharing learning across sites.
4. Arrange cover for the safeguarding champion role during their absence, so the first point of contact function is never left unfilled.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Adult Safeguarding Policy (the wider framework the safeguarding champion supports) and the Safeguarding Training Levels Guidance (governing the Level 3 training this role requires).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates that only the title has changed. A care assistant notices something that concerns them but is unsure whether it meets the safeguarding referral threshold. They raise it informally with the site's safeguarding champion, who provides the same experienced first-point-of-contact support the role always has, under its new name.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Adult Safeguarding Policy (a serious complaint alleging abuse is also a safeguarding concern) and the CQC Notification Procedure (relevant where the underlying event is also notifiable).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the tightened window. A family member telephones on a Sunday evening alleging a resident was treated roughly during personal care. This is immediately recognised as a serious complaint, and the on-call structure ensures the Quality Lead is informed within the new 2-hour window, a noticeably faster standard than the previous version's 4-hour allowance for exactly this kind of out-of-hours scenario.

Frequently asked questions

**Why was the escalation window shortened?** A review found that a 4-hour window occasionally meant the Quality Lead learned of a serious complaint later than ideal for coordinating an immediate response; 2 hours closes that gap. **Does a serious complaint also need to go through the routine complaints process?** Yes, the urgent escalation runs alongside, not instead of, the normal complaints process.

Training and competency

All staff who might receive a complaint, including reception, are shown how to recognise a serious complaint and the tightened 2-hour escalation route during induction.

Monitoring and compliance

Escalation timing is reviewed by the Quality Lead for every serious complaint against the new 2-hour standard, with any breach investigated as its own compliance matter.

Closing note

A fast, reliable escalation route for a serious complaint protects a resident and reassures a worried family, and the tightened window in this version exists to make that speed even more dependable.

Spiritual and cultural needs

A resident's spiritual or cultural wishes for this period, including any specific practice around the time of death, are recorded as part of the advance care plan where known, and staff support access to a chaplain, faith leader or cultural practice the resident or family requests wherever practicable.

Involving other residents sensitively

Where other residents in a shared living area are aware that a fellow resident is receiving end of life care, staff respond to their questions or distress sensitively and honestly, at a level appropriate to what that resident wants to know, rather than avoiding the subject entirely in a way that can leave other residents more anxious, not less.

Environmental comfort during end of life care

Simple environmental adjustments such as a preferred room temperature, favourite music, familiar photographs or objects, and minimising unnecessary noise or interruption, are arranged wherever practicable, since these small details can meaningfully affect a resident's comfort and dignity during this period alongside the clinical elements of their care.

Record keeping and retention

Advance care plans, DNACPR forms and related records are retained in the resident's care record per the Records Retention Schedule.

Approval and review history

This policy was originally approved by the Chief Executive on 1 November 2024 and this version took effect 1 June 2026, superseding the earlier version's section order.

Closing note

Good end of life care is one of the most important things Alderbridge does, and this policy exists to make sure a resident's own wishes, properly understood in advance, guide every decision made during this period; the reordering in this version aims to make the document easier to use in the moment it matters most, without changing what it actually says.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the dual-review standard. A resident suffers a fall resulting in a hospital
admission on a Saturday afternoon. The on-call registered manager drafts the CQC notification, sends it to
the on-call Quality Lead for review within the hour, and the reviewed notification is submitted that evening,

Frequently asked questions

**Why was the dual review introduced?** A review found a small number of draft notifications contained
factual gaps that a second reviewer would have caught before submission; the dual review closes that gap
for every notification, not only complex ones. **What if the registered manager is unavailable when a
notifiable event occurs?** The deputy manager drafts the notification in their place, and it still passes

Training and competency

Registered managers and deputy managers complete CQC notification training, refreshed every two
years, updated to cover the dual-review workflow and the shortened DoLS timeframe.

Monitoring and compliance

Notification timeliness and completeness is reviewed quarterly by the Quality Lead, now also tracking
dual-review turnaround time as its own metric, with any missed or late notification or review investigated as

Notification records, including the Quality Lead's review sign-off, are retained in the site compliance file per
the Records Retention Schedule and made available to a CQC inspector on request.

Stock discrepancy investigation

Any stock discrepancy identified at a weekly count is investigated the same day by the registered manager, checking administration records first before considering whether an ordering or delivery error explains the gap, since most discrepancies trace back to a simple recording error rather than a genuine loss.

Supplier and pharmacy relationship management

The registered manager reviews the supplying pharmacy's own performance annually — accuracy of deliveries, responsiveness to urgent-flagged orders and clarity of its own electronic record-keeping — since a reliable pharmacy relationship is itself part of maintaining an accurate stock position.

Handling a resident's own brought-in medication

Where a resident is admitted with their own medication already dispensed, this is checked against the GP or hospital discharge letter, recorded in the electronic ordering system as an opening balance rather than a new order, and either used down before the next pharmacy order or returned to the family if it does not match the current prescription, so that the stock record reflects genuine holdings from the point of admission rather than starting from an assumed zero.

Seasonal and holiday-period ordering

Around a bank holiday or a period when the pharmacy's own delivery schedule is reduced, the senior carer raises the relevant order in the electronic ordering system earlier than the normal weekly cycle to avoid a late Friday order arriving after a reduced-service weekend, since running short over a holiday period is harder to correct quickly than during a normal week.

Closing note

Accurate medication stock records exist to protect residents from both under-supply and unnoticed loss, and the move to the electronic ordering system exists to make an accurate, timely count achievable without relying on retrospective paperwork to close the gap.

Waste storage area security and access

The designated external storage area is kept locked between collections, with the key held by housekeeping and the registered manager only, since an accessible waste storage area presents both an infection-control and a safeguarding risk if a resident or visitor were able to access it unsupervised.

Contractor licensing checks

The registered manager confirms the waste contractor's own environmental permit or licence is current before each new contract period, keeping a copy on file alongside the electronic consignment note system's own contractor record, since using an unlicensed contractor would leave Alderbridge liable for a waste duty-of-care breach regardless of the contractor's own conduct.

Bulky and furniture waste

A bulky item such as a bed frame, mattress or wardrobe removed during a room turnover is scheduled for a separate bulky-waste collection rather than left in the general waste storage area, since the standard collection is not equipped to remove large furniture items and doing so would obstruct access for other waste streams; this stream is not part of the weighed clinical waste route introduced in this version.

Closing note

Correct waste segregation is a simple, everyday practice with a real infection-control consequence when it goes wrong, and the move to weighed, electronic consignment notes in this version exists to make an unusual pattern visible sooner, not to change how segregation itself is done.

Mobile Device Management Policy

*Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2024. Withdraws the bring-your-own-device allowance for roles accessing resident health records; those roles now require a company-issued device only.*

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group manages mobile devices, including phones and tablets used to access resident records or care systems. It applies to every company-issued device and, for roles not accessing resident health records, every personal device approved for work use.

Policy statement

A mobile device that can access resident information is managed to the same security standard as an office computer, and for roles accessing resident health records specifically, only a company-issued device is now used, so that resident data remains protected wherever it is accessed from.

Definitions

**Company-issued device** a phone or tablet provided by Alderbridge and enrolled in the mobile device management system before use. **Approved personal device** a staff member's own phone or tablet, approved by IT and enrolled in the same system, now used only under a bring-your-own-device arrangement for roles not accessing resident health records. **Enrolment** the process of registering a device in the mobile device management system, applying required security settings before it can access any Alderbridge system.

Roles and responsibilities

**IT** enrols every device, company-issued or approved personal, before it is permitted to access any Alderbridge system, confirms which roles require a company-issued device under this version, and can remotely wipe a lost or stolen device. **The device user** reports a lost or stolen device to IT immediately and never disables the security settings the enrolment process applies. **The registered manager** approves which staff roles require mobile access to resident systems at their site and confirms which of those roles now require a company-issued device.

Training and competency

Why the financial abuse agency routes were added

Following the Safeguarding Policy (Overarching)'s own formal recognition of financial abuse within its
suite, a review found this protocol's external agency list did not yet reflect the specific agencies relevant to
a financial abuse concern beyond the local authority safeguarding team itself; the Office of the Public
Guardian and Action Fraud routes close that gap, giving staff and the Safeguarding Lead a complete
picture of where a financial abuse concern might appropriately be referred.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the new routes. A concern arises that a resident's attorney has been making
financial decisions inconsistent with the resident's own known wishes and apparent best interests. The
organisation-level Safeguarding Lead refers to the local authority safeguarding team per the standard
route, and separately refers to the Office of the Public Guardian given its specific statutory power to
investigate and, where necessary, remove an attorney acting outside their proper authority, illustrating how
the two referrals complement rather than duplicate each other.

Frequently asked questions

**Does a financial abuse concern always need referring to both the local authority and one of the new
specific agencies?** Not always; the Safeguarding Lead assesses which agency or combination is
genuinely relevant to the specific concern, though a serious concern often benefits from more than one
route being pursued. **Why is Action Fraud relevant to a care home resident?** An older or vulnerable
resident is sometimes specifically targeted by a scam or fraud, including one involving a caller
impersonating a trusted organisation; Action Fraud is the appropriate national reporting route for this kind
of crime specifically.

Learning from a multi-agency safeguarding review

Where a multi-agency review identifies a lesson relevant to Alderbridge, the organisation-level
Safeguarding Lead ensures that lesson is considered against this protocol and the wider safeguarding
suite.

Appendix: information sharing agreement template

Where Alderbridge and an external agency work together repeatedly on a resident's case, a short
information sharing agreement is put in writing, recording: the specific purpose the sharing serves; which
categories of information will be shared, now explicitly including financial records where the Office of the
Public Guardian or Action Fraud is involved; how it will be transmitted securely; how long it will be retained;
and the named contact at each organisation.

Case study: coordinating with the NHS safeguarding team

A resident is admitted to hospital following an injury sustained in circumstances that are not yet clear. The
hospital's own safeguarding team raises a concern with the local authority and separately contacts
Alderbridge to request the resident's recent care notes. The organisation-level Safeguarding Lead liaises
directly with the NHS safeguarding team to agree a joint understanding of events before the resident
returns to the home.

Case study: coordinating with the Office of the Public Guardian

A concern arises that a resident's attorney has been withdrawing funds inconsistent with the resident's
known wishes. The organisation-level Safeguarding Lead refers to the local authority safeguarding team
and, in parallel, to the Office of the Public Guardian, providing factual records of observed spending
patterns; the OPG's own investigation subsequently leads to the attorney's authority being reviewed.

Cross-border safeguarding for a resident moving between local
authority areas

Where a resident transfers between two Alderbridge sites in different local authority areas, and a
safeguarding concern, including a financial abuse concern, is already open or arises shortly after, the
registered manager at the receiving site contacts both local authority safeguarding teams and, where
relevant, the Office of the Public Guardian, which operates a single national process unaffected by the
resident's change of local authority area.

genuine, well-coordinated partnership with external agencies, now explicitly including the Office of the

Definitions

**LADO** the Local Authority Designated Officer. **Safeguarding Adults Board (SAB)** the statutory
multi-agency board. **Regional manager liaison role** the coordination function supporting a multi-site or
complex concern. **Office of the Public Guardian** the new external agency route, introduced in this
version, with statutory powers to investigate a concern about an attorney or deputy acting outside their
proper authority. **Action Fraud** the new external route, introduced in this version, for reporting a
suspected fraud against a resident.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** reports a safeguarding concern to the registered manager immediately. **The
registered manager** makes the initial external referral decision, now including a financial abuse concern's
specific new routes where relevant. **The organisation-level Safeguarding Lead** coordinates the most
complex situations, including a financial abuse concern requiring Office of the Public Guardian or Action
Fraud involvement, and attends the local Safeguarding Adults Board.

Self-neglect** a resident's own inability or unwillingness to care for themselves or their environment to a degree that risks their health or safety, now explicitly recognised within this suite. **Multi-agency information sharing** the principles governing what safeguarding information Alderbridge shares with an external agency such as the local authority or police.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** reports a safeguarding concern immediately, including a self-neglect concern, following the specific procedure relevant to the type of concern. **The registered manager** leads the response to most safeguarding concerns. **The site Safeguarding Champion**, referred to consistently by this title throughout this version, provides local expertise and support. **The organisation-level Safeguarding Lead** oversees the suite and coordinates multi-agency information sharing per the new appendix.

Historical development of the safeguarding suite

The six safeguarding principles

Alderbridge's safeguarding practice is grounded in the six nationally recognised safeguarding principles: empowerment, prevention, proportionality, protection, partnership, and accountability. registered manager** makes the initial external referral decision, now including a financial abuse concern's

complex situations, including a financial abuse concern requiring Office of the Public Guardian or Action

Purpose and scope

Policy statement

A safeguarding concern is rarely resolved by Alderbridge acting alone; effective safeguarding depends on
genuine, well-coordinated partnership with external agencies, now explicitly including the Office of the

proper authority. **Action Fraud** the new external route, introduced in this version, for reporting a
suspected fraud against a resident.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** reports a safeguarding concern to the registered manager immediately. **The
registered manager** makes the initial external referral decision, now including a financial abuse concern's
specific new routes where relevant. **The organisation-level Safeguarding Lead** coordinates the most
complex situations, including a financial abuse concern requiring Office of the Public Guardian or Action
Fraud involvement, and attends the local Safeguarding Adults Board.

Fraud as explicit external agency routes for a financial abuse concern, aligning with the Safeguarding
Policy (Overarching)'s own formal recognition of financial abuse.

Purpose and scope

This protocol sets out how Alderbridge Care Group works with external agencies to protect a resident from
harm, now explicitly including the agency routes relevant to a financial abuse concern. It applies to every
site and every member of staff.

Policy statement

A safeguarding concern is rarely resolved by Alderbridge acting alone; effective safeguarding depends on
genuine, well-coordinated partnership with external agencies, now explicitly including the Office of the
Public Guardian and Action Fraud for a financial abuse concern, aligning this protocol with the
Safeguarding Policy (Overarching)'s own formal recognition of financial abuse within its suite.

Definitions

**LADO** the Local Authority Designated Officer. **Safeguarding Adults Board (SAB)** the statutory
multi-agency board. **Regional manager liaison role** the coordination function supporting a multi-site or
complex concern. **Office of the Public Guardian** the new external agency route, introduced in this
version, with statutory powers to investigate a concern about an attorney or deputy acting outside their
proper authority. **Action Fraud** the new external route, introduced in this version, for reporting a
suspected fraud against a resident.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** reports a safeguarding concern to the registered manager immediately. **The
registered manager** makes the initial external referral decision, now including a financial abuse concern's
specific new routes where relevant. **The organisation-level Safeguarding Lead** coordinates the most
complex situations, including a financial abuse concern requiring Office of the Public Guardian or Action
Fraud involvement, and attends the local Safeguarding Adults Board.

the initial external referral decision, now including a financial abuse concern's
specific new routes where relevant. **The organisation-level Safeguarding Lead** coordinates the most
complex situations, including a financial abuse concern requiring Office of the Public Guardian or Action
Fraud involvement, and attends the local Safeguarding Adults Board.

1. Report any safeguarding concern, including a financial concern, to the registered manager immediately.

2. Refer to the local authority safeguarding team within one working day for a concern meeting the local
threshold, including a financial abuse concern per the Resident Finances and Appointeeship Policy's own
Safeguarding Lead-first escalation route.

3. Refer to the Office of the Public Guardian where a concern involves a resident's attorney or deputy
potentially acting outside their proper authority; this is a new specific route introduced in this version.

4. Refer to Action Fraud where a concern involves a suspected fraud against a resident, such as a scam or
coercive financial exploitation; this is a new specific route introduced in this version.

5. Contact the police immediately for a concern involving a criminal offence, a missing resident, or an
immediate risk to life.

6. Complete a post-referral review within 10 working days of any external referral, including a financial
abuse referral to a new agency route.

raised at any site, a change from
the previous version's Finance Manager route, and coordinates with the Finance Manager on the financial
record aspect once a concern is raised. **Care staff** record every transaction involving a resident's
personal allowance at the time it occurs, never relying on memory to reconstruct it later.

1. Record every transaction involving a resident's personal allowance at the time it occurs, countersigned
by a second staff member where the amount exceeds the site's low-value threshold.

2. Reconcile each resident's personal allowance balance weekly against the transaction record,
investigating any discrepancy the same day it is found.

3. Escalate any financial concern to the Alderbridge Safeguarding Lead without delay; the previous
escalation route to the Finance Manager alone has been replaced, since a financial concern is treated
primarily as a safeguarding matter.

4. Where Alderbridge holds an appointeeship, use benefit income only for the resident's own benefit,
keeping a clear, itemised record distinct from the site's own operating funds.

5. Never accept a gift, loan or financial favour from a resident or their family that could be seen to influence
care, regardless of how it is framed.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a resident wishes to make a genuinely voluntary, modest gift to a staff member (for example, a
small thank-you at a significant occasion), the registered manager records this and confirms with the
Finance Manager that it falls within the modest-gift threshold, since this routine confirmation does not itself
constitute a financial concern requiring Safeguarding Lead escalation.

escalates directly into) and the Records Retention Schedule (governing how long financial records are
kept).

Worked example

reloaded_rendered_text:
Escalate the discrepancy to the Alderbridge Safeguarding Lead as the first contact — the policy replaces the previous Finance Manager-first route and requires immediate escalation to the Safeguarding Lead for a financial concern.

Finance retains responsibility for the financial-record and audit aspects: the Finance Manager is brought in to support the financial record review once the Safeguarding Lead has taken the concern forward, and resident fund transaction records, appointeeship files and audit findings are kept per the Records Retention Schedule; the Finance Manager also audits resident fund records quarterly.

Use the organisation-level Safeguarding Lead as the role name on the card for internal escalation, and include the external agency sharing routes now specified for financial abuse concerns — namely referral routes to the Office of the Public Guardian (where an attorney or deputy may be acting outside their authority) and to Action Fraud (for suspected fraud or scam); also retain the local authority safeguarding team referral route where the local threshold is met.
